cross-013.answer: The Skiff port runs Tern at the Performance preset (dec-run-tern-on-skiff-at-the-performance-preset--74eqayfa83ybqpe3), which saves 1.8 ms over Quality (2.1 ms vs 3.9 ms, per fnd-tern-costs-3-9-ms-at-quality-and-2-1-ms-at-perfo--dkbskbqfgfwtryq0). The lowest preset, Ultra Performance, exists only for the Meridian 120 Hz mode (dec-ship-four-tern-quality-presets-adding-ultra-perf--3jg1wyq3bshv839c).

cross-015.answer: Two Efforts are no longer active. Shader compile cache and build farm (eff-shader-compile-cache-and-build-farm--6xeac11zxvwwarkn) completed, since its retrospective fnd-retrospective-on-the-shader-compile-cache--9rpv2a60ach04cx6 says the cache has run on every farm build for five weeks. Co-op rollback netcode prototype (eff-co-op-rollback-netcode-prototype--n5ejm416kfcfap49) was abandoned via dec-abandon-rollback-netcode-for-co-op--46envrg0v4pdwv7b, because re-running tide simulation on each rollback frame costs 4.8 ms on Skiff.

netcode-004.answer: Rollback re-runs the tide simulation on every rolled-back frame, which costs 4.8 ms on Skiff (about a fifth of the 25 ms frame), and co-op needs tides to stay bit-for-bit deterministic, so the prototype was abandoned (dec-abandon-rollback-netcode-for-co-op--46envrg0v4pdwv7b). The reason depends on the world Decision dec-run-the-tide-simulation-in-32-32-fixed-point--c5rjfcnmhne4h05e.

ports-012.answer: Because saltglass caustics shimmered badly at the 540p floor, even with Tern: 7 of 10 dune views showed visible shimmer, dropping to 2 of 10 at 576p (fnd-saltglass-caustics-shimmer-at-the-540p-floor--0aa8sts89vhq1s6q), which led to the 576p decision (dec-raise-the-skiff-dynamic-resolution-floor-to-576p--fep9q7m08pp9f0bb). That decision was later superseded by the 504p floor (dec-lower-the-skiff-dynamic-resolution-floor-to-504p--15esnt90gcn29enn).

ports-013.answer: Ship Tern as Lantern's only upscaler

render-031.answer: Alpha-tested foliage cost 2.1 ms in the visibility buffer versus 0.8 ms in forward+, so it moved to a forward pass (dec-visibility-buffer-for-opaque-geometry-foliage-an--gvnvp04jgm7kbfh9, citing fnd-alpha-tested-foliage-costs-2-1-ms-in-the-visibil--f3g34x2k6fs367eb). Saltglass moved out because it refracts the scene behind it and so needs that image resolved first, which the buffer cannot provide.

render-032.answer: The team chose Tern because Halcyon has no Skiff build, and shipping it on two platforms would break the one-upscaler constraint; owning Tern's code also lets them make saltglass refraction and caustics fixes the same week instead of filing closed-binary vendor tickets, with no license to negotiate. (dec-ship-tern-as-lantern-s-only-upscaler--fmreq35nzyjc7k4e)

render-046.answer: The cost Finding that had sunk virtual shadow maps was a capture error; with cached pages VSM costs 1.4 ms, less than four cascades, and cascade seams through saltglass remain unsolved under CSM (record dec-use-virtual-shadow-maps-for-the-sun--x8nqkn9q7eaf1ap4, reopened 2026-01-12 from its rejection by dec-use-cascaded-shadow-maps-with-four-cascades--s5c1y9jaf275afzr).

render-047.answer: It brought the visibility buffer back to Skiff because its release-build capture measured 7.4 ms against 8.1 ms for forward+ (6.3 ms with half-rate material resolve), so the forward+ fallback was no longer worth keeping, and maintaining two opaque paths cost about one engineer-week a month (dec-visibility-buffer-on-all-platforms-skiff-resolve--k1ackk3c3275r5y1).

world-036.answer: Kestrel retired the fiber scheduler because 41% of alpha crash reports had no usable stack, which blocked crash triage for beta, and a continuation-wait thread pool kept workers 93% busy during tide turns, close to the 95% fibers gave (dec-return-engine-jobs-to-a-thread-pool-with-continu--1zkc1v2x97taf50h).

world-051.answer: Float tides drifted apart between machines within 6 minutes, with PC against Skiff the worst pair, from fused multiply-add contraction and a Skiff sin() one ulp off (fnd-float-tides-drift-apart-between-machines-within--znd0wy18bfw2prss); fixed-point integer math gives identical bits on every CPU and compiler, with no platform math library, so the tide runs in 32.32 fixed point. Record: dec-run-the-tide-simulation-in-32-32-fixed-point--c5rjfcnmhne4h05e

world-055.answer: Kelp stays because shrinking its dictionary to 1 MB made it beat Zstandard cold on Skiff (2.2 vs 1.3 GB/s, 1.7x), per dec-shrink-kelp-s-dictionary-to-1-mb-for-streamed-as--yh8hktfqnyqhepew. After Skiff firmware 3.2, the 1 MB Kelp still wins (1.5 vs 1.2 GB/s), per fnd-kelp-with-a-1-mb-dictionary-decodes-at-1-5-gb-s--y9v8jrxgbv6abrx5.
